questions.question: How does this repo implement API versioning -- URL-path based, header based, or both -- and what drives the choice across 10+ domain APIs?

genesis.observation: All domain API directories follow the pattern api/{domain}/v1/ (aviation, climate, conflict, consumer-prices, displacement, economic, forecast, giving) -> versioning strategy is a core architectural convention that must be understood

questions.question: How are the 6+ specialized Dockerfiles (digest-notifications, publish-bootstrap-tiers, relay, seed-bundle-*) deployed -- are they separate microservices or different entrypoints into a monolith?

genesis.observation: Repo has 6+ Dockerfiles (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.digest-notifications, Dockerfile.publish-bootstrap-tiers, Dockerfile.relay, Dockerfile.seed-bundle-portwatch-port-activity, Dockerfile.seed-bundle-resilience-validation) -> deployment topology is complex and needs clarification

questions.question: How does the batch processing pipeline (api/batch/v1) handle data reliability -- exactly-once semantics, retry strategy, and dead-letter handling -- given it coexists with real-time API endpoints?

genesis.observation: api/batch/v1 directory suggests batch processing capability alongside real-time REST endpoints -> data pipeline reliability strategy must explain both synchronous and asynchronous data flows

questions.question: Why are 10+ unrelated domain APIs (aviation, climate, conflict, cyber, economic, giving, etc.) aggregated into a single service rather than decomposed into independent services with dedicated backends?

genesis.observation: Diverse domains (aviation, climate, conflict, consumer-prices, cyber, displacement, economic, forecast, giving) all live in the same repo with no obvious per-domain backend separation -> cross-domain aggregation is a non-obvious architectural decision that needs evaluation

questions.question: What is the Brief service's role in this architecture -- given its complex nested routing (userId, carousel, issueDate, public) and its position as the most structurally elaborated API module?

genesis.observation: api/brief has 4 sub-paths (userId, carousel/userId/issueDate, public) making it the most complex API module in the repo -> Brief appears to be the core product experience and deserves focused analysis

questions.question: Why is Discord OAuth (api/discord/oauth) directly embedded at the same architectural level as first-party domain APIs rather than abstracted behind a generic authentication gateway or plugin system?

genesis.observation: api/discord/oauth exists as a top-level API alongside domain APIs like api/aviation, suggesting a specific platform integration is baked in rather than abstracted -> authentication architecture may lack extensibility

questions.question: Why is REST chosen over GraphQL for this multi-domain API -- given that 10+ heterogeneous data domains would benefit from a unified query layer to avoid over-fetching and under-fetching?

genesis.observation: All domains exposed as REST endpoints with no GraphQL or BFF layer in the directory structure -> REST vs GraphQL is a significant design space for multi-domain APIs that needs justification

questions.question: Is the resilience validation (Dockerfile.seed-bundle-resilience-validation) covering actual runtime failure scenarios like cascading failures and partial outages, or is it limited to synthetic pre-deployment smoke tests?

genesis.observation: A dedicated resilience-validation Dockerfile exists but the name suggests seed/bundle (pre-deployment) rather than runtime circuit-breaking -> resilience testing may not reflect production failure modes

questions.question: If a new domain API (e.g., api/healthcare/v1) needs to be added, what is the exact file change set required -- and what existing abstractions reduce or amplify the onboarding friction?

genesis.observation: api/[...notfound].ts catch-all handler exists alongside explicit api/{domain}/v1/ directories, suggesting a tension between convention-based routing and explicit onboarding -> maintainer cost for adding new domains is unclear

questions.question: Can a single API service correctly handle both real-time geopolitical event data (conflict, cyber, displacement) and batch economic time-series data (forecast, consumer-prices, economic) without compromising on either's data model?

genesis.observation: Real-time geopolitical data (api/conflict, api/cyber, api/displacement) and batch economic time-series data (api/forecast, api/consumer-prices, api/economic) coexist under the same API convention -> data model tension between event-based and time-series is an unresolved architectural question

alternatives_considered: Unified data model with type discrimination
